text:
maria: quick sync — I'm seeing a weird regression when continuous-batching is enabled + prefix cache. p95 hop up ~30% on short prompts, hit-rate stable-ish but end-to-end latency worse.
sam: Can you paste numbers? which model/quant/profile?
maria: r-instruct-7b, int8 w/ kernel v2.3. profiling yesterday: cache hit-rate 62% (+2%), but p50 42ms -> 58ms, p95 120ms -> 160ms. tokens/s down ~8%.
julian: that smells like batch composition causing more cache-miss latency amplification. when miss lands in big batch it stalls others.
maria: exactly. observed queueing spikes in the timeline: batch size jumps then KV warmup ioctl spikes.
nora: did you check kernel selection path? v2.3 changed tiled-gemm fallback for short seqs, might affect small-token latencies.
maria: yes — kernel trace shows more codepath switches mid-batch. we get extra memcpy for KV for some seq-length combos.
sam: hmm. two levers: 1) batch scheduler that prefers matching prefix keys (coalesce by cache-key hash) 2) eager prewarm for likely prefixes. both have tradeoffs.
julian: coalescing sounds promising but could hurt fairness. if we wait to coalesce we add queueing latency. numbers?
maria: rough sim: if scheduler waits up to 8ms to coalesce, hit-rate up to 72% and p95 drops to 130ms. but p50 up ~+5ms from wait. if no wait, hit-rate 62% and p95 160ms.
nora: that's the classic latency vs hit-rate tradeoff. maybe dynamic timeout based on load could help: short timeouts under low load, zero under high load.
infra-bot: incident note created: INC-2026 - prefix-cache/continuous-batch latency regression (auto-created from perf alerts)
maria: another idea: key-aware batching where we inject a tiny affinity token to influence batch composition without waiting. basically soft-affinity in scheduler.
sam: can you sketch config? something like:
```
batching:
  max_wait_ms: 4
  key_affinity_weight: 0.2
  affinity_buckets: 64
```
maria: yes, that. affinity_buckets = 64 worked in local sim: +7% hit-rate with <3ms avg extra wait.
julian: also look at KV warmup scheduling. current warmup runs when miss occurs, blocking the request thread while kernel allocs happen. should be async when safe.

nora: async warmup needs careful memory/eviction policy. if we prewarm too many keys we increase memory pressure and slow kernels.
maria: true. we tried speculative prefetch for top-K prefixes per customer (based on traffic) — reduced miss tail but increased GC churn.
sam: what about hybrid: prewarm only on worker spare cycles and maintain a small ready-queue for hot prefixes.
julian: add telemetry: tag each batch with composition fingerprint (dominant-prefix, mixed-prefix) and log latency per fingerprint. we currently lump everything.
maria: added a proto event in trace: batch.fingerprint and kv.warmup_time. will push today.

nora: also check kernel selection thresholds: v2.3's tiled-gemm chooses path when seq_len>=16 or token_count>256 per batch. continuous batching changes token distribution; thresholds might be stale.
sam: good point — scheduler changes the effective seq distribution due to prefix joins. we should re-run the kernel selector autotune under continuous-batch load.

maria: action items:
- julian: prototype key-affinity scheduler + optional max_wait_ms (2d)
- nora: async kv-warmup POC and memory guardrails (3d)
- sam: re-run kernel selector autotune under simulated cont-batch traces (this week)
- infra-bot: keep INC-2026 open and attach traces

sam: fine. small note — keep experiments reproducible: capture batch composition heatmaps and seed traffic replay.
julian: will add heatmap export to perf harness.
maria: thanks everyone. if anyone wants to join pairing later ping me. :thumbsup:
sam: pinged — I'll join at 11:30
nora: dropping in for kernel tuning.
